chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Mithamī, from Ibrahim ibn Mihzam, from a man, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), when the meal was raised, would say: 'O Allah, You have increased [the provision], made it pleasant, and blessed it, so You have satiated us and quenched us. The praise is for Allah who feeds and is not fed.'
ai.seo_question: What is the supplication recited after eating a meal in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Prophet’s (peace be upon him) practice of thanking Allah for the abundance and quality of food, emphasizing gratitude for both physical sustenance and sensory pleasure. It underscores the Shia scholarly view that daily acts like eating are opportunities for spiritual elevation, linking the material act of dining with the recognition of Allah as the ultimate Provider who feeds but is not fed. This supplication serves as a model for transforming mundane routines into acts of worship through mindful remembrance.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad Bin Al Hassan Al Maysami, from Ibrahim Bin Mihzam, from a man, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, whenever the meal was raised, said: ‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! You<sup>azwj</sup> Made it plentiful, and pleasant, and Blessed, so You<sup>azwj</sup> have satiated us, and quenched us. The Praise is for Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Who Feeds and is not fed’.
en.sarwar: 15. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Ahmad ibn al-Hassan al-Mithamiy from Ibrahim ibn Mehzam from a man who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has stated this Hadith. ‘

The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, when the table was moved would say, “O Lord, you have granted a great deal, have made it very good, blessed it, made us satisfied and quenched. All praise belongs to Allah who feeds and is not fed.’””
